# Asymptotic Notation (MIT 6.006 Lecture Notes)
Definition & Core Mechanics:
Definitions of Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta for runtime bounds. In algorithmic analysis, we evaluate worst-case performance under the Random Access Machine (RAM) model where standard arithmetic and pointer dereferences take constant O(1) time.
Key Properties:
1. Space Complexity: Auxiliary memory overhead required during execution.
2. Invariants: Formal inductive invariants that guarantee correctness throughout execution.
3. Optimal Substructure: Decomposing larger problem instances into smaller identical sub-instances.
When applying Asymptotic Notation, consider edge cases such as empty inputs, duplicates, and boundary limits. Consult CLRS Chapter 1 for full proofs.
